subject: Performance SLO follow-up: latency/throughput targets + cost levers (Orion AI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orion-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: latency/throughput targets + cost levers (Orion AI)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups to make sure our perf qualification aligns with your production goals so we can bake accurate cost estimates into the proposal.

Recap of requirements I heard on the call:
- Target tail latency: p95 <= 150 ms for single-shot text generation (avg prompt length ~120 tokens)
- Throughput target: sustained 200 req/s during peak windows, 1k req/s bursts for short periods
- Concurrency: expected concurrent users ~20-30 sessions, with session streaming required for partial responses
- Streaming: yes — we need token-by-token streaming to the client (SSE/websocket)
- Accuracy: prefer model variant with top-2 quality hit vs larger model

Couple of questions to finalize sizing/cost levers:
1) Are you ok with a slightly higher p95 (200 ms) if we can keep the tail predictable via continuous batching and prefix caching?
2) How tolerant is your product for model-variant fallbacks (e.g., 13B quantized primary / 7B fallback) during capacity pressure?
3) Any constraints on quantization or model weight residency (e.g., must be int8, or ok with int4)?
4) Can you share a typical prompt distribution (short/medium/long) and percent streaming sessions vs single-shot?

Attached: I dropped a quick workbook with a few capacity profiles and cost levers (continuous batching thresholds, caching hit assumptions, and sample quantization cost estimates).

Next steps: if you can answer the 4 questions above, we'll run a small perf-sim and get back with a recommended config (kernels, batching window, caching policy) and a P50/P95 cost estimate. Also proposing a 30-min follow-up Wed 3/18 to review.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orion_latency_requirements.xlsx, redwood_slo_cost_levers.csv

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orion-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orion-ai.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: latency/throughput targets + cost levers (Orion AI)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Answers inline and a few clarifications below.

1) p95: Our initial product KPI is p95 <= 150 ms but for launch we can accept p95 <= 200 ms for short windows if you can guarantee graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model + sticky cache).
2) Model fallback: Yes — we prefer a primary quantized model and an automatic fallback policy. Important: falls back only on sustained overloads, not bursty transient spikes.
3) Quantization constraints: int8 is preferred for our safety/regulatory team. Int4 is okay for non-sensitive inference paths but we'd like performance/regression tests.
4) Prompt distribution: ~60% short (<50 tokens), 30% medium (50-200 tokens), 10% long (>200 tokens). Streaming: ~40% of sessions require streaming (chat UI).

Additional notes:
- Peak concurrency target: 25 concurrent sessions, average session requests ~8 requests/session/min during active use
- Data residency & encryption: all inference must run in us-west region and keys via our KMS; we'll share access for testing

I attached our latency matrix and a draft SLA for your review (SLA-draft-v1.pdf). Looking forward to the perf-sim.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform
Orion AI

Attachments: SLA-draft-v1.pdf, orion_latency_requirements.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: latency/throughput targets + cost levers (Orion AI)

Looping in my notes for the perf-sim and suggested cost/performance levers given Orion's answers:

- Batching: Use continuous batching with a short max latency window (8-12 ms) to preserve p95 while improving throughput. For their short-heavy prompt distribution, batching will yield >2x token efficiency.
- Caching: Prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts and user prefixes — assume 25-30% cache hit (they have a lot of repeated templates). Sticky session cache for streaming sessions to reduce repeated KV warm-ups.
- Quantization: Recommend int8 for primary production model (13B) — balance of quality and memory. Offer int4 7B variant as fallback in overloads. Need to run regression evals on Orion's prompt set; plan: 1k sample evals with our eval harness.
- Model variants & routing: Primary route to quantized 13B in us-west GPUs; fallback route to 7B quantized in same region with fast warm-start. Add policy: graceful degrade with notification to app when fallback active.
- Autoscaling: prefer predictive scaling based on traffic patterns + small burst buffer for 1k req/s peak bursts.

I'll prep a perf-sim template (kernel choices, batch sizes, expected p50/p95) and a cost delta table for int8 vs int4. Marissa — can you confirm we have KMS access during their eval window?

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the speedy answers and attaching the SLA. Next steps from our side:

1) We'll run a perf-sim matrix (Rishi) and share P50/P95 latencies across the candidate configurations (13B int8 primary / 7B int4 fallback; batching windows: 8/12/20 ms; caching assumptions: 15/30% hit). Expect deliverable by end of day 3/19.
2) Priyom will coordinate KMS access & test credentials (Priyom: can you confirm timeline?).
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync Fri 3/19 at 11:00 AM PT to review perf-sim and recommended config. I'll send a calendar invite.

If that all looks good I'll incorporate the recommended config into the commercial proposal and show the cost delta for int8 vs int4.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
